newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Labour says to cut debt to 22 pct GDP by 2000.
newsitem.headline: NZ Labour says to cut debt to 22 pct GDP by 2000.

text.p: New Zealand's opposition Labour Party said on Thursday its policies would lead to a fall in net public debt to 21.8 percent of Gross Domestic Product by the year 2000.
Finance spokesman Michael Cullen released the party's fiscal model in the light of last week's pre-election update from Treasury.
Labour plans a slower rate of debt repayment than the current National Party government and higher investment in health and social services.

Labour sees the government's consolidated operating balance, which was $3.31 billion in 1995/96, easing to $2.74 billion in 1996/97, $1.99 billion in 1997/98, $1.47 billion in 1998/99 and $2.64 billion in 1999/00.

From 1997/98 onwards, Labour projects surpluses to build in its proposed dedicated superannuation fund. The consolidated operating balance of $2.64 billion in 1999/00 would include a superannuation fund surplus of $1.19 billion and an operating

Last week's Treasury forecasts, assuming no change from current policies, projected operating surpluses of $2.87 billion in 1996/97, $3.39 billion in 1997/98, $4.70 billion in 1998/99 and $6.42 billion in 1999/00.
The Treasury forecasts showed net public debt falling to 13.3 percent of GDP by 2000.
Cullen said the figures released by Labour showed its policies were clearly affordable.
"This shows that much greater investment can be achieved in health, education and social services while still having the strongest net debt reduction programme of any developed country," he said.
